v.rationale: All three pass their own suites (impl-2: 22, impl-1: 19, impl-3: 11). All three send the email only after the outer transaction commits, so a rollback, including a savepoint rollback, sends no email and adds no points. impl-2 ranks first. It claims the order with a single atomic UPDATE, which also covers the stale-instance case, and resyncs only the status attribute. The staff check is a policy applied through `can` middleware, and its tests are the broadest, including stale instance, owner-forbidden with an invalid body, and 401 with and without an Accept header. Its main idiom cost is a domain exception that extends an HTTP exception. impl-1 is nearly identical in design and has the cleanest exception-to-409 mapping (in bootstrap/app.php) plus a good unique-constraint rollback test. However, `syncOriginal()` marks every attribute clean, and a probe confirmed this silently drops unrelated unsaved changes on the caller's model. That is a real data-loss risk for the back-office callers the task mentions. impl-3 is correct for the HTTP flow. It ranks last because it maps the 409 with a try/catch in the controller, does the staff check in FormRequest::authorize instead of a policy, uses lockForUpdate (a no-op on SQLite) with a read-then-write, and leaves the caller's model dirty. Its tests are also thinner (no 404, stale-instance or rounding edge cases), and it deleted the base app's example tests. In-memory status staying Shipped after an outer rollback is a minor issue all three share.
